title: Judge command substitution by position, not by pattern
claim: A shell-command audit must classify by syntactic position: value position captures output, command position executes; an interpreter's code-string flag is an execution context wherever it appears; heredoc bodies are data. Pattern matching on the text cannot make that distinction.

title: Personalization does not pay; recurrence does
claim: A personal skill performed about as well as one borrowed from a stranger, and a generic skill built from many developers beat both. Personalization looked promising only when a preference recurred across similar tasks.

title: Silence is not completion once a marker protocol is live
claim: Once the injected marker protocol reports a command started, only the completion marker, a timeout, or the stream ending finishes the run; idle-based completion stays correct on the fallback path but its completion authority does not survive promotion to the protocol tier.

title: A durable log may not claim liveness
claim: A persisted "this is running" flag is unfalsifiable after a crash, so the reducer's output carries no status field at all and consumers derive state from suspension, terminal and outstanding records.

title: A weight penalty attached to the act of correcting
claim: The write path applies target.weight - 0.1 to the new row on a correction, so ten unattended corrections drive a claim to zero and a well-maintained record becomes indistinguishable from an untrusted one.

title: The transcript is the protocol, not the render surface
claim: A streaming row's prefix can be committed early on a re-renderable scroll container and cannot on irreversible native scrollback; replay is an exactly-once history with a resize policy, not a bounded ring for re-attach.

title: Guards get mechanised by syntactic locality, not artifact shape
claim: Both of the source's conventions are artifact-shaped, and only the syntactically local one got a guard: a log macro within 24 lines is a window scan, while 'this unwrap is unreachable from network input' is a call-graph reachability property. The mechanisable region is narrower than prose-rule-drift says.

title: Consolidation stops paying once the reader can hold the mess
claim: A measured null at about 50 sessions: consolidation merged real duplicates and bought no accuracy, because the reader could still hold the unconsolidated store.

title: Recall precision scales with fact granularity, not count
claim: Recall precision may scale with item granularity rather than item count (~10 tokens per fact, 50 facts is 500 tokens; embrace a little noise); the discriminator would be fact atomicity.

title: Namespace claimed by shape; host reserves the unmarked remainder
claim: The extension namespace is claimed by SHAPE, not by enumeration: a trailing underscore marks "mine" and everything unmarked is reserved to the host, including names the host has not invented yet. Validated in one comparison on the last byte, warns with the repair named, and openly accepts no inter-extension collision protection.

title: The expensive mode is a property of the input part, not the request
claim: An expensive-processing switch is set per input part, so one request can mix modes across its parts and its cost is not characterized by a single mode.

title: Bounded failure memory beside unbounded success memory
claim: The failure lane is bounded and silently drops its oldest entries while the success lane never forgets, so the store forgets exactly the evidence a diagnosis needs.

title: A resolvable citation to a derived artifact is verifiable and empty
claim: Every citation in the generated wiki resolves, and each points at a projection of a generated summary of a prefix of a flattened clone - so a citation audit passes while the evidence chain is empty.

title: A canary enrolled in the judged population inverts its own retention rule
claim: A fuzzer that fails on seed % 100 == 0 is scheduled alongside the real ones, a PR job must carry the canary and one real fuzzer, and the retention rule is inverted for it - prefer newer seeds for canaries to show it is alive, older seeds for the rest to keep them stable - with duration dropped from the canary's ordering because it obscures timestamp_start.

title: Assertion discipline as a subject with a density floor
claim: Density of at least two assertions per function; pair assertions on two different code paths (before write and after read); assert positive and negative space; split compound assertions; keep assertions on in production because it is far better to stop operating than to continue in an incorrect state; and a control plane may spend O(N) verifying an O(1) data-plane operation.

title: Containment maturity does not imply accountability maturity
claim: 83% of the coded corpus has at least process isolation, 40% has no audit trail at all, and only 5% is tamper-evident - so isolation maturity predicts nothing about accountability maturity.

title: Delegation creates a context-persistence obligation
claim: File persistence is present in 85% of orchestrator-worker projects against 20% of single-agent ones, so introducing delegation creates an obligation to persist context rather than merely an option.

title: The concurrency ceiling is supervisory, not machine
claim: Ten to fifteen live threads are bucketed into priority folders because a human tracks about four or five concurrent things; the human tracks buckets, not threads.

title: A skill that writes a hook has mutated your harness
claim: An installed skill that writes a hook has changed the harness itself, not the prompts - so installing a skill is a configuration mutation with a different blast radius from adding instructions.

title: A producer-reported line count measures its edit grammar
claim: AI lines must be counted by reconstructing each file version from its baseline and diffing, because whole-file-rewrite edit tools re-serialize the body (over-count) and ranged-replace tools only show insertions (under-count); comparing models or harnesses by 'lines written' otherwise measures their edit grammar.

title: Trust analysed-tree executable rules by content hash
claim: Personal and project rule files whose DSL executes when the dashboard opens are trusted on first use by SHA-256 of their content, any edit revokes approval, blocked files queue for review, and user regexes pass a backtracking heuristic and an input cap - because a cloned repository can ship a rules directory that runs when the reader opens a view.

title: Similarity is not an equivalence relation over ownership
claim: buildClusters clusters on cosine alone, never comparing scope or category; buildMergedEntry takes members[0].scope with the comment 'all should match'; the header asserts 'validated upstream' and the production caller passes undefined for scopes; sources are hard-deleted with no tombstone, so the one lifecycle operation that destroys evidence is also the one that ignores ownership.

title: A display label must never be the dispatch discriminator
claim: transportConfig.kind is the routing contract and category is display only, because the display taxonomy correlates strongly with the transport family - which is what makes it a tempting dispatch key - but grouping labels change for UI reasons and transport families change for protocol reasons, at different rates and by different people.

title: Pick the patching mechanism, and price it against distribution
claim: Four strategies chosen by dependency shape (fork-and-submodule, mirror shadowing, runtime hooking, compile-time IL weaving); runtime IL injection was abandoned for compile-time weaving not for correctness but for distribution, because runtime injection trips antivirus heuristics and the modified assemblies cannot inherit the application's signature.

title: Ship a linter for the contract the type system cannot hold
claim: The repo ships eight lint rules which read together are not eight rules about a library but a taxonomy of the type system's blind spots: key order in an object literal, referential identity of a returned object, which fields a consumer read, whether a function returned anything, the lifetime of a container - every one a contract term a compiler cannot hold and whose violation is silent.

title: Inclusion patterns rot, and in the opposite direction
claim: entry-empty, entry-redundant and entry-top-level are non-suppression configuration rot with the opposite error direction from a stale suppression: an inclusion pattern that matches nothing, duplicates another, or is trivially broad silently widens or narrows the root set rather than hiding a known finding.

title: Never execute a consumer's config to read it
claim: Executing a consumer's configuration file to read it inherits that file's environment-variable dependencies and crashes on configurations that are valid in production; the tool's arc ran execute then static AST between 2025-02 and 2026-03.

title: A cheap downstream observable corrects a weak classifier
claim: Stop raising classifier accuracy and instead place a cheap observable downstream that catches the error after the fact: if a fix misclassified as a small issue ends up being 500 lines of code, force-reclassify it as the other one; the stated sufficiency target for the classifier is 60 percent.

title: framework-stewardship as a subject nobody scopes
claim: Four existing subjects each explicitly scope away from adopting a framework version across a fleet - supply-chain scopes to trust crossings, build-economics to the cost of iterating, perf-instrumentation to the product measuring itself, multi-project to portfolio management - and candidates 1, 2, 3 and 6 of this run all land in that seam.

title: The oracle predicts the rejecting rule, not the verdict
claim: A model-based oracle over a 52-million-case matrix predicts which of 37 rejection rules fires, and the suite fails on four distinct mismatch kinds - unpredicted accept, unpredicted reject, unknown classification, and the wrong rule - so an unclassifiable rejection is itself a finding.

title: Wait for the readiness marker, not the first protocol sighting
claim: Shells emit a stray completion marker and a prompt-start marker during startup, so a detector that trusts any marker declares the protocol available before the line editor accepts input and the first command is lost.

title: Emit a readiness marker after the mode it advertises is enabled
claim: A readiness marker emitted from the prompt string arrived while the parser still saw bracketed-paste mode disabled, so the detector believed a capability that was not yet there; the marker moved into a line-editor init hook that runs after the input mode is actually on.

title: single-flight's five honest options are missing a sixth
claim: One shared computation per equivalent request, where a deadline-bound waiter preempts and continues it: the frame thread never blocks behind background work, the running thread's priority is raised, and plain join and plain recompute were both rejected.

title: Make a stale derivation unaddressable instead of migrating it
claim: INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION = "5" is the search index's own name, so an index written under an older schema is not detected as stale, it is unopenable, and the load path clears the directory and rebuilds.

title: A copy regime whose copies cannot be generated
claim: Facts are stated in N places on purpose, N is enumerated, one copy is named authoritative, and the drift check is a reviewer rather than a generator - because the copies are prose in different registers for different readers and are not mechanically derivable from one another.

title: Pre-resolve resources a synchronous engine cannot await
claim: The async layer parses the query text to pre-resolve every sandboxed-filesystem handle the synchronous engine will need, and drops them in a finally, because the engine cannot await mid-execution.

title: Producer and consumer conformance are decoupled on purpose
claim: "There is no implied relationship between document conformance requirements and implementation conformance requirements. User agents are not free to handle non-conformant documents as they please; the processing model applies regardless of the conformity of the input." The producer's rule set is a freely-revisable subset of what the consumer must accept forever.

title: Invalid on purpose, to reserve extension space
claim: "attributes in end tags are ignored currently, but they are invalid, in case a future change to the language makes use of that syntax feature without conflicting with already-deployed (and valid!) content." The gap between what you refuse to emit and what you must accept is the extension budget.

title: Trust tiers inside one instruction file, with an anti-forgery clause
claim: Sections of one instruction file are declared universal, maintainer-only, local-machine-only or external-contributor, each gated on machine-verifiable conditions, plus an anti-forgery clause.

title: Injected caller context is inherited by children
claim: The runtime injects session and pane identifiers into the environment, so a nested launch silently addresses the parent; the mitigation unsets the whole set per command.

title: A guard that is present, registered and inert
claim: Four artifacts look maintained and do nothing: a compatibility hook whose dtype_map raises NameError into a bare except so every frozen build ships unpatched, an event with zero subscribers leaving a whole coalescing path inert, a generated client headed do-not-edit that nothing imports beside a hand-written one, and a helper referenced only by its own test.

title: An experimental namespace does not preserve design freedom
claim: A separate experimental namespace does not preserve design freedom: consumers write both forms side by side, pre-emptively, before the real syntax is final - a measured historical refutation of a plausible mitigation.

title: Replaceability and trustworthiness are inverse goals
claim: A runtime in which an agent can replace the component that records what the agent did has made the recording layer answerable to the thing being recorded.

title: Two session identities, half the state each, silent re-thread
claim: Two session identities each own half the state - the host transcript mirrored per turn, the provider thread map held in the adapter - and a failed resume silently starts a new thread.

title: Confinement as the default answer, denial as the escalation
claim: An unmatched shell command runs in the OS sandbox rather than prompting, and a kernel denial escalates to a human who may re-run unsandboxed - while an unavailable sandbox returns ALLOW unsandboxed although the docs promise ASK.

title: A central tier table when the rows sum into one pool
claim: One central tier table is the only form that can express the constraint when four models compete for one allocation, and the tree states the coupling in the offload threshold's own comment.

title: Sender override when the receiver's adaptation only ratchets up
claim: The receiver's adaptive buffer grows on jitter and never shrinks, and three named receiver-side knobs cap the floor without pulling a ratcheted buffer down, so the sender stamps an authoritative override on every packet.

title: Elide by producer class, never by output size
claim: Source-like and arbitrary output returns unchanged, search results are reorganized losslessly, and only predictable repetitive noise is compressed - because a size threshold compresses exactly the outputs most likely to be re-read.

title: One store, three read doors, three caps, no marker
claim: Three read paths take 20, 50 and all rows respectively and none of them marks the truncation, while the same codebase emits an explicit truncation marker elsewhere.

title: Minimal escaping needs lookahead across the assembly seam
claim: Context-sensitive minimal escaping needs lookahead across the output-assembly seam, and an unknown context must revert to conservative escaping.

title: Depth staging is decided before any optics
claim: Nothing in the corpus places objects in depth, so a depth-of-field clause has nothing to act on when the near plane is empty, and the sensation of speed comes from differential parallax across depth layers rather than from a speed adverb.

title: Invert the release level by blast radius
claim: Additive changes take a patch and repairs to existing utilities take a minor, because new features pose no risk to existing code while fixes change how it works.

title: An acquired asset is an origin the gate cannot represent
claim: Given web access and no sourcing policy the agent downloaded third-party animation and image packs on its own; a downloaded asset is a served reference with no generation history, no producer evidence and a licence, and the gate's three-valued origin field reads it as generated.

title: A configuration failure must not take the runtime fallback
claim: The verb refuses when no model is configured, before the extractive-fallback branch, even though a non-empty gather would have produced a good degraded answer - because that answer would mask the misconfiguration forever.

title: Roster size is priced in wall clock, not tokens
claim: A tool roster cut to five essential tools went from about twice a competitor's wall clock to 36.6s against its 42.2s, median of 6 runs with a fresh session each, because tool grammar constrains the token generation process and not just the prefix.

title: Guarded post-decode correction, against a landed rule
claim: Post-decode fuzzy vocabulary correction as the fallback for engines without decode prompts, with four guards - a 25% length ratio, a punctuation boundary, no phonetic boost for numerics, ASCII only.

title: A fourth warmth point that is not a point in time
claim: Warmth taken from a sibling entry's payload, and a seeded key that collapses a waterfall rather than a spinner; its cost is that the source entry's key coordinates become part of the consumer's addressing contract and vanish silently on a deep link.

title: Failure-taxonomy counters beside the pass rate
claim: The benchmark scores pass/fail and separately counts syntax_errors, indentation_errors, lazy_comments, exhausted_context_windows, test_timeouts, num_error_outputs and num_user_asks, so two runs with an identical pass rate are still diagnosable into prompt, format or model.

title: One core, three doors, no privileged agent path
claim: The HTTP, WebSocket and agent faces are thin projections of one service, and the first-party agent gets no privileged path, enforced by there being no other door.

title: An ephemeral queue that supersedes a durable design
claim: The pending queue was made ephemeral, reversing a committed durable design, because a durable queue would promote at startup and begin model calls nobody asked for; the accepted cost - a remote sender's queued message lost silently on a crash - is recorded beside the decision.

title: Cite the commits that exist only because a rule was skipped
claim: The rule carries a retrievable commit list as its origin - "Commits 7a7e87d9, 6bd85a3f, 73341f4f exist only to paper over this being skipped - do not add to them" - a re-measurable predicate whose growth refutes the rule.

title: Preflight measures resources from the runtime's own vantage
claim: A container reports its own CPU and RAM, not the host's, so preflight measures the wrong machine; and the instruction-set check is skipped under one hypervisor because cpuinfo lies there, collapsing could-not-determine into healthy, justified by a loud first-use failure.

title: Two environments disagree, cause unisolated - quote the lower number
claim: "We had previously reported... over 50% faster. On Kubernetes we measure a larger OLTP gap, 50-60% rather than 30%, and we have not isolated why the same binaries behave differently there than on bare EC2, so we quote the lower number."

title: Triage verification targets by circuit structure, not input size
claim: "SAT cost tracks the arithmetic circuit structure, not input-space size (all proofs quantify over full 2^32-2^96 spaces; that part is free)." A 2,547-word measured cost model with a named wall taxonomy and a remedy per class.

title: Go see the stakeholder's operation before proposing anything
claim: Learn the stakeholder's operational reality first-hand before proposing - the container-terminal truck ride, where the constraint turned out to be $50k/hour at 12% capacity.

title: Generate a hermetic per-workload agent config
claim: Every session is fresh and runs against a generated agent config with no tool servers; the interactive profile booted three npx tool servers per session, took over 20 minutes with no request reaching the model and left 63 MB per directory, while the generated config starts in about 10 seconds.

title: Emitted code must not touch the caller's namespace
claim: The generator opens its own scope so it binds nothing the caller can see, and refers to everything it needs by absolute path so it depends on none of the caller's imports.

title: The printed plan is an upper bound, not a prediction
claim: The execution plan builds the whole step vector up front while the per-step condition is decided at run time, so --print-steps prints steps that may never run and nothing marks which.

title: The same license boundary drawn twice, opposite and both correct
claim: GPL dictionaries ship as data inside the AGPL package, while GPL capture code stays behind a socket in a separately-licensed directory - two opposite conclusions about the same boundary, each right for its case.

title: Arm a child-side orphan guard against host death
claim: The child receives the parent's pid at spawn, arms a guard before anything that can block, and kills its own process group when the parent is gone; the entry names three known gaps (killed before init, shell nodes that never init, one platform).

title: Write last, read first when two stores share no transaction
claim: When composing two systems with no shared transaction, order the writes so the observable intermediate state is safe and read from the authority; the sequential composition of two transactions is not itself a transaction, with idempotency as the precondition.

title: Review as a commit of code comments on the branch
claim: Code review is a single commit on top of the PR branch, threads marked `//? resolved`, concluded by an explicit revert commit so the review is preserved in history; limits stated: hunk-boundary conflicts and force-push friction.

title: Gate exceptions name consumer, rationale and an issue
claim: Gate-exception allowlist entries must name consumer, rationale and a linked issue; malformed entries fail closed; exceptions cannot suppress a deleted test or an added `.skip`.

title: A deliberate forget blocks re-derivation, an expiry does not
claim: An operator-issued forget must suppress re-derivation of a key so the next cycle cannot reverse the correction from the same episodes, while an expiry must not; a store with one forget operation cannot express both.

title: A stub aborts naming its library; NOP only for registration APIs
claim: A link-time stub aborts loudly and names the library it stands for rather than returning a plausible default, because reaching it at runtime means the test's dependency graph is wrong. A second form prints SKIP and continues, reserved for registration-pattern APIs where the result cannot affect the test, and the two-way split is made once at the stub definition.

title: Additive is unsafe for a generated typed client
claim: Even a new optional field is breaking within a frozen contract version, because a generated typed client's reader surface is derived rather than written and does not degrade gracefully on an unknown field.

title: Guard SSRF at the persist door with stable machine-readable reason codes
claim: SSRF is guarded at the persist door on both the watched URL and the webhook URL, with stable machine-readable reason codes the HTTP adapter keys on - never the prose, which embeds host values and can be reworded - and a test pins the adapter's key set against the code object so wording drift cannot silently break status mapping.

title: A seven-adapter variance map with message identity broken two ways
claim: Seven transport adapters were mapped for variance and message identity is broken in two distinct ways across them, each at a named line.

title: An efficiency mode's saving is paid on the latency axis
claim: Time to first token rises on short inputs because of the mode's own reasoning loop, so the mode carries a duration precondition stated as a number - under five minutes, use static processing.

title: Cold-start tax is route-independent, about eleven round trips
claim: The fixed boot cost falls out of differencing two recorded phases and is about eleven round trips regardless of route; no column in the instrument reports it.

title: A wildcard is a valid non-empty allowlist granting everything
claim: The same privilege is enforced more weakly in the less-isolated mode, and a wildcard entry satisfies every non-empty-allowlist check while granting everything.

title: Delegate by net benefit; default to direct execution
claim: Delegation is decided by net benefit with direct execution as the default, and the hard vetoes are inter-agent output dependencies and overlapping mutable state.

title: A total delegation cap beside the concurrency cap
claim: A per-run total delegation cap is needed beside the concurrency cap, because repeated legal-sized batches issued at planning checkpoints bypass a per-response limit.

title: Stamp message provenance unconditionally at the producer
claim: Provenance is stamped at the producer whether or not an observer is installed, because "a fact whose presence depends on whether an observer is installed is not a fact"; server-owned keys strip forged provenance.

title: Exit-0-with-no-edits marks a source consumed
claim: An ingest marks a source consumed on agent OK even when no edits were made, so a silently unproductive pass is recorded as success and the source is never revisited.

title: Make the release cheap enough to skip
claim: Skipping a release is an explicit design purpose: when a PR feels like it must land, land it at its natural pace and skip the release instead; the changelog still merges under an unreleased header and version numbers stay monotonic with gaps.

title: A bounded ledger that keeps failures and carries dropped work forward
claim: At most 32 commits and 4 seeds per commit-fuzzer pair; prefer failing records, prefer faster failures as coarse minimisation, prefer older for stability; and when dropping a passing record add its count to a survivor so the aggregate work total is preserved.

title: A ban carries its replacement
claim: Every banned construct is paired with the thing to use instead, grouped by why (stdlib wrapper provided, library footgun, language footgun); the linter exempts itself and vendored code by explicit path; and the whole rule set is snapshot-tested.

title: A predicate-gated capability reports its absence as nonexistence
claim: When a capability is gated on a predicate the compiler reports a failed bound as "no such method" rather than "this exists but your bound failed", so the diagnostic hides the real cause.

title: A fleet sweep must reconcile against in-flight fixes
claim: A per-customer sweep gathers activity and errors since the last sweep, ranks the top three, then checks each against open and merged PRs before reporting.

title: Unattended capacity buys defect work, never selection
claim: Overnight capacity runs bugs and triage, not product: no frontier model has the intelligence to know what to ship, and automatic improvement loops do not work with product.

title: Attribute nothing on ambiguity: evidence precedence for work-item credit
claim: AI credit for a work item comes from sessions linked by evidence precedence - a workspace created from the item, else a pasted link, else a single referenced item, else NOTHING - and a session naming two items gets neither; per-item estimates count a shared session fully in each row while the total dedupes sessions.

title: The deterministic half of an ML decision fails loud at boot
claim: Narrow a probabilistic component's authority to the inference only: the roster is declarative data validated fail-loud at boot and an invalid arm panics the process, so the failure class is removed rather than monitored - after a measured incident where the roster-catalog binding dropped unknown IDs silently and one inert arm sent 19.8 percent of balanced-cluster turns to maximum-tier arms, 821 dollars of that cluster's 1,022.

title: Artifact-kind placement routing for an instruction system
claim: A four-way taxonomy - always-loaded rule, on-demand skill, subagent, tool-server - with per-kind admission criteria (rules over 100 lines or carrying code examples belong as skills; skills marked always-apply belong as rules; agents without example triggers or with unnecessary tool access are anti-patterns) plus a context-impact estimate over the always-applied set.

title: Hide the overlay from the layer that queries, not from the mouse
claim: The overlay is made invisible to the accessibility layer by setting a window property that layer's own traversal reads, rather than by being made transparent to input, because the standard hit-test API is global and returns the topmost element - which is the overlay itself.

title: An overlay perturbs the system it observes
claim: Treat the overlay as a perturbation of the thing being observed, not merely as an occluder of it: a browser-engine application watching for opaque occluders hibernates its renderer and reparents the accessibility provider out of the window subtree being queried, so the query returns only a root element and the cause is invisible from the query site.

title: Protocol detection is not a permanent verdict
claim: The protocol path keeps the heuristic fallback for mid-execution loss, because history expansion, a user rc file, or a script error can swallow the command-start marker after detection already succeeded.

title: An injected integration re-converges its invariants every cycle
claim: The wrapper rc sources the integration script and then the user's own rc, which can override history and prompt settings, so the injected integration re-establishes its invariants on every prompt cycle rather than once at startup.

title: A generator's viable rate is a property of the target
claim: One pipeline inside one company spans 20 percent viable tests in Java, 40 in Go and 80 in Python, so a generator's viable-output rate is a property of the target ecosystem rather than of the generator; a pilot's rate is not transferable and adoption is decided on a locally measured number.

title: Entry points hide in shell strings and CI YAML
claim: Entry points hide in shell command strings and CI workflow YAML, not only in source, so a complete module graph needs a bash parser plus per-launcher argument grammars.

title: Every pipeline stage ships its measured accuracy with the change
claim: You have to push repros onto the system, so you actually have to give metrics for every single version of this pipeline - a stage change arrives with its own measured accuracy or it does not arrive.

title: One framework version across a fleet
claim: One member sat a minor behind five siblings and the six manifests carried three exact pins and three caret ranges for the same dependency; cross-repo dependency coherence is owned by nobody.

title: One neutral default cannot serve a composite term and a veto
claim: A degraded utility call defaults to 0.5, above any plausible veto floor, and the suite pins that behaviour deliberately; the neutral default is right for the composite score and wrong for a feature that also holds an absolute veto, so one number serves two uses.

title: Choose hook arbitration by the answer's cardinality
claim: resolveImport is first-plugin-wins and short-circuits; transformImport folds over every plugin. A specifier has exactly one correct target so a second opinion is a conflict, while the specifier's text carries orthogonal rewrites that genuinely compose.

title: Queue and collapse is a fifth interruption answer
claim: The framework waits for pending transitions to finish and animates the next from B to D, so intermediate states never animate; a flushSync toggle measured 0 animations.

title: Animation direction comes from the cause, not from a state diff
claim: Navigating a carousel forward to slide three and backward to slide three both set currentSlide to 3, so wrap-around is the falsifier for any direction inferred from a before/after index.

title: A path deny guards one tool's door; the shell reaches the same bytes
claim: Path-bound deny rules are per-tool guards, and the harness extended then reverted the shell's reach across 2.1.257/259/260, so a deny on a path does not deny the bytes.

title: One API surface, per-transport guarantees, absence rather than denial
claim: A WebSocket remote honours the protocol shape but none of the sandbox guarantees, and the loss is enumerated per property; separately, dangerous capabilities do not exist in the VM rather than being blocked, and the names are removed from the bundled typeshed so type checking rejects before runtime.

title: A glyph and a null both read as verdicts they had not earned
claim: The suite forbids checkmark-prefixed strings that present a platform capability as verified, and separately requires both agent-facing instruction files to state that a null backend value is a safety state rather than a routing instruction.

title: A carried artifact's manifest with symbolic input constraints
claim: The bundle specification carries symbolic shape constraints (`spatial_shape: ["*", "16*n", "2**p*n"]`), a required_packages_version list with "later versions expected to work", and declared post_processed_outputs.

title: A global seed does not reach objects that own their RNG state
claim: set_determinism "will not affect the randomizable objects ... which have independent random states", and 1.6.0 replaced global RNG calls with instances.

title: Audience-scoped projection from one source, and the view that stopped building
claim: Per-span inclusion attributes cut four audience editions from one document, with a substitute-definition mechanism for anchors in excluded spans - and the operating doc records the bill: "for a long period the developer's edition was not working and so we made a lot of changes without properly considering their impact on it", a derived view neither removed nor fixed, with the debt now undiscoverable.

title: A linter over prose: declared variable scope with a named escape
claim: Variables in specification algorithms are scope-checked by the build - an unscoped variable is an error, a variable used exactly once inside an algorithm is a warning, and an explicit ignore suppression exists.

title: The feature cost ledger, and who does not pay it
claim: Eleven enumerated costs of adding one platform feature - implementation, tests, QA, refactoring, tutorials, cognitive load, reduced exploration, page maintenance, spec writing, bug fixing, binary size - almost none of them paid by the proposer.

title: A mismatch must veto, not merely fail to boost
claim: A scorer that only adds evidence for agreement merges on absence of evidence; disagreement has to veto.

title: A kwargs catch-all silently downgraded a persistent store to in-memory
claim: An unrecognised configuration key was swallowed by a **kwargs catch-all, so the store ran in memory while presenting as persistent.

title: Frame caps are per payload class, not one global
claim: Three caps by payload class - 2 MB default, 32 MB graphics, 16 MB clipboard - rather than one global frame limit.

title: Optional schema fields decay while features depend on them
claim: signals is populated in 18 of 193 records and anti_patterns in 3 of 193, against a specification that builds a Compare view and a Decision Explorer on both.

title: Bound the enrichment wait, and keep cold start out of it
claim: A rival blocks the edit tool up to 5s for diagnostics and can additionally pay a 45s initialize on first touch, with a LATENCY-CRITICAL comment on its own early-resolve path; this source caps at 1.5s and warms reads in the background.

title: Every degradation names itself and its remedy
claim: A rival surfaces "[Skill conflicts] description exceeds 1024 characters (1089)" at first paint; this source silently truncates at 300 and the user never learns their skill is broken.

title: Multi-hop scenarios built only from linked contexts
claim: A multi-hop generated question draws its contexts only from node pairs joined by an entity-overlap or summary-similarity edge, and the overlapped entity becomes the bridging theme.

title: Exact determinism is claimed from the request, not from a replay
claim: Pinned temperature 0 and seed 42 through a local OpenAI-compatible server split on one case across five identical requests, reproducibly, while stamped exact - so "a replay reproduces" cannot be the definition of exact.

title: A delay constant where a human and the machine race
claim: A ten-minute auto-payment delay makes the machine wait for a human who may be paying the same invoice on a hosted page, with no shared key, no shared row and no lock either party can join.

title: The version overlay is not the migration boundary
claim: A per-organization rollout flag, not the v1/v2 route split, decides which pricing model is authoritative, and the enforcement is mounted on the old surface - 403 on writes, reads left open.

title: The overlay's exit condition is a parity spec
claim: A set-difference assertion over the router keeps v2 a superset of v1 forever, so the overlay ends on a proven parity rather than on a date.

title: A retry budget measured in event age
claim: The retry budget is measured in event age rather than in attempt count, and a parse failure commits immediately.

title: A perimeter inspector's oversize default is allow
claim: The inspector reads a bounded prefix - 16 KB by default, raisable to 64, fixed at 8 KB on two surfaces - and its oversize handling defaults to continuing with what was inspected, so an oversize request is allowed rather than flagged.

title: Never merge a server-assembled filter with a caller-supplied one
claim: Assemble the filter server side and never merge it with a caller-supplied filter, because the combination logic then becomes a security control and combination logic is where these bugs live.

title: Train and serve round the final window differently
claim: Training splits already-encoded features with floor while serving encodes a short segment with ceil, so the last window carries an extra frame and no lookahead - off-distribution exactly where the sequence ends.

title: A fourth trigger-puller guarded only by MAY
claim: Server-supplied code that calls server tools and writes the model's context is a fourth party able to pull a trigger, and the specification guards it only with MAY.

title: Greying out an irreplaceable user artifact
claim: This tree greys out and auto-corrects incompatible options, which a game-production technique forbids; the discriminator may be that the hidden objects are irreplaceable user artifacts.

title: Do not merge tables whose columns have opposite permitted values
claim: Two tables share a shape and are deliberately not merged because one column's permitted values are opposite - a refinement pass must never touch a reference sample, because cloning breaks unless the text matches verbatim.

title: Never review a stale branch through a two-dot diff
claim: Never review via main..HEAD, because a squash computes diff(head, merge-base) and an unrebased branch's squash reverts in-between work.

title: Proposal volume is not method diversity
claim: 98 percent of proposed sycophancy methods used one published technique, so 150 attempts can be one method.

title: Correct colour drift downstream, baked into the artifact
claim: Independently generated assets are not mutually consistent in colour, and the economical fix is a downstream deterministic correction baked into the artifact rather than a regeneration or a better prompt.

title: A sensor that ran, matched, then abandoned the file
claim: A sensor that ran, matched, then abandoned the file mid-stream is a third state, not a skip - the search stopped prematurely.

title: A dependency's introspection API decides its host's optimizations
claim: The alternate regex engine exposes no syntactic-analysis API, so a whole-buffer optimization is unavailable and every search falls to line-by-line - the dependency's introspection surface, not its speed, bounds the host.

title: An eligibility predicate before the process is spawned
claim: A per-file external hook needs an eligibility predicate evaluated before the process is spawned: 0.138s to 0.008s on the tool's own repository, because the spawn is the cost, not the work.

title: Shield high-salience members from a legitimate consolidation
claim: Consolidation must shield high-salience members with non-redundant signals - activation, an absolute-confidence floor and betweenness centrality - each named as catching what the others structurally cannot.

title: Freeze the threshold at enqueue, read the kill switch at drain
claim: A deferred pass judges against a threshold frozen when it was enqueued while an operator can still stop it mid-flight through a live kill switch.

title: An update notice is information, never permission
claim: The notice is information, not permission, silence is never consent, and the package may never quote, summarize or translate the remote manifest's summary - only a fixed local sentence.

title: Grade the weak mode, do not refuse it
claim: Same-identity verification still works and is recorded advisory rather than refused, and is never silently upgraded.

title: Offload deadline strictly before the kill deadline
claim: Two deadlines per tool call - offload (leave the foreground) strictly before kill (stop running); offload is refused without a >=30s seedable kill budget, and keeping the call in the foreground may clear offload only if a kill deadline exists.

title: A proposal carries margin and a marker of its own edges
claim: A proposal is delivered with 15-second handles before and after plus an explicit duration marker of the portion being suggested, so the reviewer can move the edge without re-deriving it.

title: Compaction failure falls through to unmarked forgetting
claim: Compaction returns the uncompacted history on exception and the token-budget enforcer then drops the oldest messages with no marker and no record, so the silent forgetting mechanism is the last line of defence and fires exactly when things are worst.

title: One win rate mixing controlled and uncontrolled observations
claim: The source implements the position-swap control correctly for disagreement and then admits an unpaired verdict at face value, so one win-rate number mixes position-controlled and uncontrolled observations.

title: Binding tests silently test the wrong artifact
claim: Four distinct instances in one repository - cwd shadowing, an offline install, a generated version guard, and cdylib harnesses excluded from the root test run - each has the binding test passing against something other than the artifact it claims to cover.

title: Constraint is conserved, not removed
claim: Pinning prompt slots redistributes the model's freedom into the unpinned ones rather than removing it, and forfeits the engine's own direction, which has value.

title: Agent bulk actions trip third-party abuse detection
claim: An agent filed 28 issues in 12 seconds and the platform banned the bot as spam.

title: The recovery path is the loss signal
claim: Instrument how often the consumer opens the saved original, reruns the command, repeats exploration, narrows searches or takes extra turns; frequent recovery means the transform removed something valuable.

title: The cost of an agent-only build, measured
claim: Agent-only cost: 1.29B and about 2.5B tokens, roughly 50-100 hours, about $40-100 of assets; a human does the car-with-doors in 30 minutes.

title: A side effect has no seam; extract the value
claim: The row was formatted inside a println! in a loop, so there was no value to assert and no test; the fix extracts format_run_row -> String and the test arrives with it.

title: A job map where one holder is displaced by numbers
claim: An engine admission bar built as a public job map: each named job has exactly one holding implementation, and a challenger takes the job by publishing better numbers.

title: A suite that cannot express the signal returns blindness
claim: A corroborating suite whose corpus cannot express the signal under test returns blindness, not confirmation - the measurement the eval doc says it currently cannot have.

title: Delta storage is not inherently ancestry-dependent
claim: The source ships deltas that are self-contained because the materialization unit is the whole session at a journal point, not a checkpoint row, so the coupling delta implies walking ancestry implies not self-contained is false.

title: Producer-cadence smoothing is not adaptive flushing
claim: The source varies the release rate of buffered content while holding the flush interval fixed, which is a different knob from the adaptive cadence render-throttling forbids; it needs the guardrails the source omits - never reorder, never drop, bypass at finalization.

title: A fifth catalog projection, on a new discriminator
claim: Bounded operation set gets a schema; open-ended operation set gets a code surface - a fifth member on a discriminator the corpus does not use, and the source projects with no external ceiling because of a latency cost the corpus does not know about.

title: When folding operations into one tool is honest
claim: A fold is honest when the operations are one operation from the caller's point of view and the variant is derivable from the arguments; dishonest when the caller must choose among them.

title: The cheapest path proves its own stability
claim: The skip path snapshots the source, finalizes, snapshots again, publishes, snapshots a third time, and falls out to the full path on any drift - the cheapest branch carrying the most proof, which inverts the usual instinct.

title: Fan-out isolation derives status per branch
claim: Fan-out isolation derives status per branch; all-failed is error, not a benign skip.

title: Two live caches over one datum: set one to zero
claim: With a router preload cache and a query client both caching one datum, set one to zero rather than tuning both - the router config delegates all caching to the query client.

title: Opt-in persistence declared on the datum
claim: Persistence opted into via typed metadata on the datum, with the narrowing predicate composed with the library's correctness filter rather than substituted for it, and a restore barrier that renders nothing until rehydration completes.

title: Memory-safety defects are invisible to a functional suite
claim: A quick sanitizer pass found issues in all C and all-but-one C++ programs that the correctness score never saw; fixing them pushes cost past the memory-safe language and still leaves lower confidence.

title: Reliability demand scales with the workflow
claim: About one rule violation per 100 rule-agent-days is fine at 10 agents with review and catastrophic at 1000 shipping unreviewed; the unit, rule-agent-days, is the reusable part.

title: Fit to your own traced workload with a trace-drawn holdout
claim: Workload-specific optimization is now cheap: fit to your own traced workload with a holdout drawn from the same trace; 2% and 7% wins for minutes of human time.

title: Locator leniency follows the anchor kind
claim: Leniency is admissible where a format identifies its target by position or context and must fail closed where it identifies by content, because a near-miss there applies an edit to code the model never looked at.

title: A monitoring feed must exclude its operator's own output
claim: Exclude your own website, so new blog posts are not found and reported back as news about you.

title: The serving endpoint is a fifth input to the embedding derivation
claim: The model NAME an endpoint answers to is not the model's identity: quantization, revision or normalization can differ behind one name, so vectors from two endpoints serving the same name can be incomparable. Condition: only when the endpoints serve different weights or preprocessing. Amendment to embedding-lifecycle, whose stamp is name+version+dimension. [wave1 c03: split out; corpus names the endpoint as a cache-key input but not this.]

title: Allowlist load failure yields an empty allowlist by design
claim: When the plugin-file-reference allowlist cannot be loaded, the provider returns an empty allowlist by design rather than refusing.

title: Customisations as patch files, so the drift gate is free
claim: Local customisations ship as patch files against shipped defaults - an overlay whose drift gate costs nothing, because a patch that no longer applies fails loudly where a merged overlay drifts silently.

title: Disclose that the published artifact is not the measured artifact
claim: "The binaries we publish are generic for their architecture. The benchmark numbers come from builds tuned for [one microarchitecture], so you will not reproduce them exactly from a download."

title: Reconstruct and pin a competitor's methodology before comparing
claim: A 1,116-word pinned methodology with fetch dates and verbatim commands, plus the explicit note that the competitor's own harness "is not public... there is no public repo with full automation or raw results."

title: Name the operating altitude before pointing an agent
claim: A roughly 17-level ladder in 5 bands (line/block/function/type/class - file/module/directory - db/table/script/CLI - application/repo/plan/docs - agent/workflow/factory), with leverage and control trading monotonically along it.

title: A seen-marker before a capped stage loses most of the work
claim: Each comment is marked seen at fetch time for up to 120 comments while extraction runs at most 3 batches of about 18 comments and skips entirely when the model server is down, so most of a thread is marked structured and never structured - on the success path, from a planned budget cap.

title: A proxy allowlist the client writes is not an allowlist
claim: The route hands the proxy an allowlist supplied by the client it is meant to constrain, so the constrained party defines its own scope.

title: Memory keyed on a typed identifier
claim: Six apps scope agent memory to an identifier the user types, so memory identity is whatever string was entered and two users who type the same string share a memory.

title: A service that moves the artifact's frame is a provider criterion
claim: One mesh service returns models out of their original position and another returns them in the same position, and some people choose the second for that alone; the cost is a manual realignment per part, so it scales with the cut plan and can invert a provider choice made on raw quality.

title: Generate in the target's own syntax, not as strings
claim: Emit code in the target language's own syntax with interpolation holes rather than assembling strings; the string form loses every tool that understands the target.

title: Pick the IR's strength from the input's contract
claim: The weak token tree is used when the input is a DSL that may not be host syntax at all; the full syntax tree is opted into only when the input is guaranteed to be valid host code.

title: Compile-time code emission as a missing subject
claim: Three mechanisms from one source share one home-if-new, and the corpus has a coherent hole: the contract between a generator and the two worlds it touches, the host compiler and the caller's lexical scope; research-map also returned a flat empty for codemod transformation.

title: Linear memory is leasable but never shrinks
claim: WASM linear memory is treated as a leasable resource with refcounted pins, and the module is discarded above 64 MB because linear memory never shrinks.

title: Admit a decode on pixels, not bytes
claim: Decode admission is checked against a pixel budget rather than a byte budget, re-checked after every transform, and computed by division rather than multiplication so the check cannot overflow into permitting what it exists to refuse.

title: Encode once, splice the envelope per recipient
claim: The payload is serialized once and the envelope is string-spliced per recipient because only the sequence number varies across recipients.

title: An ID buffer that expires so its timestamp cannot lie
claim: Pre-allocated distributed IDs are held in an age-bounded buffer and discarded after 5 s so the timestamp embedded in an ID cannot lag reality.

title: Wide-column emulation with a bounded planner
claim: A wide-column store is emulated over one physical key-value table on a relational engine, with the query planner bounded at 32,768 row-key combinations.

title: Subset fonts from ingested content, not UI locale
claim: Script-font chunks are chosen from the content the system ingested rather than from the UI locale, with document language used only as the tiebreak among Han variants.

title: Precompute the predicates an extension would have to parse
claim: The host precomputes about 15 booleans the extension would otherwise have to parse JSON to answer, and ships the JSON anyway.

title: Validate the whole set while it stays small
claim: The CI validator runs over the entire contributed set rather than the changed files, deliberately, for as long as the set stays small enough for that to be cheap.

title: The cache key is the provider-transformed body
claim: The gateway keys its cache on the body as transformed for the provider, not on the caller's request.

title: A decision carries the observation that retires it
claim: A design decision is recorded together with the observation that would retire it and the fallback it flips to: if a third strict-superset gap is ever found, the decision flips to Option B. title: A prefilter must be a provable one-sided superset
claim: A prefilter placed before a policy owner must be a provable one-sided superset of it, and its marker set is coupled to the owner's decoders as an explicit change rule, because the failure is the prefilter quietly stopping being a superset.

title: Pick a pacing primitive by its loss policy
claim: Five client-side pacing primitives are discriminated by what each does to the calls it does not run: debounce rejects during activity, throttle rejects all but one per interval, rate-limit rejects at quota, queue rejects only when full, batch never rejects.

title: A wrapper's boolean never says which half it governs
claim: Disabling the rate limiter blocks the wrapped function entirely rather than disabling the limiting, and setting the retryer to throw on every error silently disables retrying; an option on a wrapper is ambiguous between the wrapper and the wrapped, and the name resolves it in neither case.

title: A screenshot contract as a runtime obligation
claim: Because the critic pipeline sees the product only through one capture tool, the product must uphold a declared contract - a readiness global, a deterministic view enumeration, no dependence on wall-clock or input, zero console errors - or the build is defined as broken.

title: Harness memory decomposes by control function
claim: Harness memory has four components - skills, state schema, invocation policy, checkers - and the interesting claim is that retrieval policy and checkers are data the loop may edit, not code.

title: Widen reads through a mode that cannot reach a write
claim: `reach: bound | tenant` widens the owner-visibility condition for reads only; write assertions are untouched and there are exactly two construction sites, so authority is bounded by which function the mode can reach, not by a check.

title: Never recover a skip from rendered error text
claim: `missingServices` stringifies the squashed cause and regex-matches `Service not found: e2e/...`; a skip reads green, so any failure whose rendered cause contains the substring is laundered into a pass, and two always-provided services share the namespace.

title: Hard delete makes a state structurally unaskable
claim: Disconnect deletes the connection row, so a signed-out user is bit-identical to one who never connected; a dated customer flow forced a nullable status plus `status_changed_at`, with blast radius enumerated.

title: An asset bundle that carries executable code
claim: When a target tool cannot read a representation natively, the vendor bridges it with a script inside the asset bundle, and the import step silently becomes code execution inside the artist's session.

title: Stop a revision loop by where accepted updates land
claim: 39-52% of accepted updates land in iterations 0-1 across models, 39-58% across benchmarks, 33% middle / 28% late on the hardest; the curve shape (when to stop iterating) is unmined.

title: A findings report carries a per-finding verified flag
claim: The audit report as an artifact: per-finding `verified` flag, Highs adversarially re-verified, Mediums auditor-reported, an empty Critical section stated as empty, quick wins separated from deeper investments.

title: A throwing guardrail is recorded and skipped
claim: The guardrail chain is fail-open: a throwing guardrail is recorded and skipped, and blocking is explicit (`block: true`), never accidental.

title: Payload-mutating middleware defaults off, pinned by test
claim: Payload-mutating middleware defaults OFF because the operator owns the data; a regression test asserts both the definition default and behavioural pass-through.

title: First forwarded chunk is not token-level TTFT
claim: First-forwarded-chunk latency is not token-level TTFT, and the doc says so rather than letting the metric name imply it.

title: Ground the distiller in who speaks about whom
claim: The distiller is configured with entity context: picture a third person watching a conversation between two people - what do they remember, and about whom?

title: Scope the distiller's input set at write time
claim: Filter by metadata on add, so a derived fact is built only on one team's slice, instead of scoping only the query at read time.

title: AI adds a work layer and saves no time
claim: AI lands as a new work layer; nothing else shrank to make room (work-side Jevons).

title: A semantic change retires a diagnostic ID; retired IDs are never reused
claim: A log message carries a stable numeric ID keyed to its semantics rather than its text or source location; a substantial semantic change mints a new ID and retired IDs are never reused, because operators suppress and rate-limit by ID in config that outlives the binary and a suppression rule is a negative rule. [wave1 c02: split out - an ID-lifecycle rule (published register of retired IDs; suppression config outlives the binary), not text-vs-identifier. Return condition: a fleet project gains an operator-suppressible diagnostic surface.]

title: Two-sided unconditional callback obligation
claim: Callbacks must be called and unwanted calls must be cancelled; both obligations are unconditional and neither party inspects the other's liveness, because deliverability is decided by the queue at dial time. Caller-side liveness checks are rejected as a race.

title: A price arm breaks the rate comparison
claim: An experiment arm that changes the price is not comparable on conversion rate, because the arms no longer measure the same quantity.

title: Leaf dependency sink for a cyclic import graph
claim: A cyclic import graph is broken by designating a leaf module as the dependency sink that everything may import and which imports nothing.

title: A status transition is a change at equal body hash
claim: A 200 that becomes a 404 with an identical-looking body IS a change; treating equal body hash as no-change is a silent-failure mode.

title: Null the LLM-sourced field that is not literally in the source
claim: Provenance is per field: verify literal presence in the source for llm-provenance fields only, null the field on failure with a warning, and exempt heuristic and structured-data values because they are already trusted.

title: Two gates with deliberately disjoint jobs and a never-empty floor
claim: A URL-shape gate and a content gate are kept disjoint, and the content gate is explicitly NOT a relevance filter because the reranker already owns relevance; a never-empty floor keeps the single best candidate.

title: A baseline you could not capture is a dated document
claim: A skip-reasons document names the syscall that blocked the baseline, both workarounds tried and why each failed, the exact corpus, metric and output-path recipe for a host that can capture it, and a status of PARTIAL with the reason "environmental constraint, not a code issue".

title: The bootstrap tool floor as a falsifiable claim about a harness's core
claim: The harness declares a bootstrap tool floor - the irreducible set of tools a profile must have - which makes the claim about its own core falsifiable.

title: A prompt-surface inventory with a change-routing table
claim: The tree maintains an inventory of every prompt surface with a table routing a change to the surface that owns it - the note calls it the most portable artifact in the tree.

title: Route the query to the cheapest signal track, escalate on failure
claim: One artifact carries several parallel signal tracks at different token densities over one timeline (frames, audio, transcript); route the query to the cheapest track that can answer it and escalate on failure.

title: A primary-routed write in the cold path of an anonymous read
claim: A rule forbids primary-routed writes in the cold path of an anonymous read; the tree contains a live violation, recorded by the instrument and rejected by no gate.

title: Index-plan assertions with a skewed seed
claim: Assert the query plan, not just the returned rows, and seed the fixture with skewed data so the planner's choice is exercised.

title: A static export-shape check replacing a consumer-typecheck harness
claim: A static check of the exported shape replaces a harness that typechecked a consumer against the package.

title: Build error-matching patterns from the identifier constant, not the vendor's prose
claim: Match errors on the vendor's identifier constant rather than on its message text, because the prose is reworded without notice.

title: Renewal binds to the original credential, not to any currently valid one
claim: A renewal must bind to the credential it was issued against rather than to whichever credential is currently valid.

title: Request-body complexity admission beyond a byte cap
claim: Admission caps JSON memory and string count, not only request bytes, because a small payload can be structurally expensive.

title: Stamp the trace id at the trust boundary; the 500 path needs it most
claim: Stamp the trace id once at the trust boundary and carry it on every persisted and echoed surface; the unhandled-500 path is the response most in need of it and the one most likely to ship without it.

title: A subagent on the parent's thread must skip the parent's memory flush
claim: A subagent sharing the parent's thread id must skip the parent's memory flush, or its internal turns pollute the parent's durable memory.

title: A restrictive skill must list delegation explicitly
claim: A restrictive skill must list delegation explicitly to permit it; read-only discovery tools may reveal metadata but cannot widen the policy.

title: Middleware self-description as an assembly fingerprint
claim: Every behaviour-affecting field of a middleware is declared as an identity, with long text hashed, so two assemblies can be compared by fingerprint.

title: A summary of a prefix is a claim about the prefix
claim: Description generation reads 200 KB of a flattened archive and writes three to five sentences about "the project", so the summary's scope silently contradicts what it claims to describe.

title: Multiversion binaries: past releases embedded in the current artifact
claim: Past releases are embedded in the current artifact as extra binary sections; the newest version always starts and decides which to run, and the process stats its own binary on a one-second timer to learn about new versions without a restart.

title: A sampled read of a large tree must publish a coverage statement
claim: A sampled read must publish a coverage statement naming which surfaces were read closely enough to support each coded claim, plus a confidence note for ambiguous boundaries.
home: our own docs/forge-brief.md and harvest-brief.md; skills lane, no gate

title: Risk-score a change to decide if a human is needed
claim: A PR is scored on about five risk aspects including blast radius and security; low is auto-approved and merged, medium and high are routed to a named human because a compliance control requires alternative review.

title: Bound the review loop; approve an artifact cheaper than the diff
claim: A fresh review is triggered on the PR for at most two loops, then a recorded narrated walkthrough with a red/green test list is produced; the human approves the video and it merges.

title: Route local versus cloud by intervention need, not task size
claim: Local wins for large front-end grinds that need a local browser and frequent steering, and for verification; cloud takes everything else.

title: Agent thread versus public chat: the legibility discriminator
claim: One operator moved all multi-user interaction into the agent's threads for context locality; the other kept agents in public chat because that is what made them legible during company adoption.

title: A global restyle is a token audit
claim: Run a global restyle and whatever fails to change was never tokenized - the restyle is the audit.

title: Materialize subjective variants as isolated trees judged side by side
claim: When the choice is subjective, build each variant in its own isolated tree and judge them side by side rather than arguing the specification.

title: A derived artifact is never a primary source
claim: A derived artifact is never a primary source, and summarization layers compound loss.
home: strong in recruiting, civic and media bundles; thin in software-engineering

title: Signed delivery authenticates the relay, not the author
claim: The webhook key authenticates the service that delivered the event, not the author of the message inside it; once a per-agent inbox is live, anyone who knows the agent's address can wake it and write the text it reads, with a tool-holding agent that replies to them.

title: Wire-path representability filters candidates
claim: Bypass the intermediate representation when the source format equals the target family, and derive semantic requirements at ingress as hard candidate filters: the IR cannot represent extension points it does not model, and a requirement that must survive the wire path is a representability constraint, not a quality signal a scorer may trade away - a fully capable model is ineligible when the only translation to it drops the request's semantics.

title: Look for the observed subsystem's own opt-out first
claim: The team spent two chapters building a scoped replacement for a global API (reaching an unexported function by scanning the module for its telemetry trace string and walking back to the prologue past the padding) and chapter four found a metadata property in the subsystem being queried that removed the need for any of it: when the instrument perturbs the system, look for the observed subsystem's own opt-out before building a scoped replacement for its interface.

title: Infer required context by walking the condition tree
claim: Required context is inferred by walking the condition tree, so there is no requires section that can drift from the conditions that actually read it.

title: Settings are a document to patch, not a payload to replace
claim: The JSON document is the source of truth and the runtime object is patched from it, because a settings file behaves like a user document rather than a payload: whole-graph replacement drops keys written by other versions and breaks live bindings. Prune is opt-in per subtree.

title: Review depth as a function of change metadata
claim: Verification depth is a pure function over change metadata, with security-path globs forcing the top tier regardless of size.

title: A file-drop verdict channel applied by role, not capability
claim: Foreign-runtime workers return verdicts by writing a JSON file the leader polls, and the verdict is applied by role rather than by capability; a worker that disagrees writes 'revise' rather than exiting silently.

title: Await-shaped ergonomics serialize independent work
claim: Await-shaped fetch ergonomics serialize independent work, so concurrency needs a plural primitive rather than a loop over the singular one.

title: Search consumers' committed config before removing a feature
claim: Measure a feature's adoption by code-searching consumers' committed configuration before removing it, and publish the query so the measurement is reproducible by the people it affects.

title: A fixture must lie outside the fallback's reach
claim: A fixture must lie outside the fallback's reach or the test measures the fallback: use non-default file names so the test actually verifies resolution.

title: Calibration is bidirectional; a refusal is a recorded output
claim: Calibration runs in both directions and leave-unchanged is a first-class recorded output: a capability repeatedly proposed for promotion and always refused reveals an unspoken constraint, and one nobody proposes to move is a removal candidate.

title: Advisory rail precedence by re-emittability
claim: Advisory rails arbitrate by precedence rather than order: a once-only advisory speaks and a repeating one defers, because the repeating one will get another turn and the once-only one will not.

title: The flow channel needs breathing room
claim: The flow channel needs breathing room; constant escalation is its own failure mode, not a maximally engaging one.

title: Findings form causal chains, not N independent bugs
claim: Findings form causal chains - unused file, then unused exports, then unused dependencies is one cause and not N bugs - so a report that counts them separately inflates its own total.

title: The result unit is (browser x file), immutable inside a mutable manager
claim: The same file can pass in one engine and fail in another, so a file-level result cannot represent the run; sessions are immutable and the manager that holds them is mutable, which lets reporters observe transitions without owning them.

title: The interop escalation ladder, where the ordering is the content
claim: Six strategies in an explicit preference order for shipping against an ecosystem gap: find an ESM distribution, ask the author, find a fork, write a UMD wrapper, use a converting CDN, transform at serve time.

title: Gate a unit's reveal on its media, not only on its data
claim: Wrapping images or fonts inside a transition boundary triggers Suspense while they load, so the reveal waits on media that arrives after the data.

title: A lifecycle hook runs from a cwd it does not own
claim: Harness lifecycle hooks execute from a working directory the hook did not choose, so paths must resolve from the project-root variable (2.1.239).

title: Judge the asset in its delivery context, not on a neutral rig
claim: The creator re-imports each asset into the engine to judge it under the project's lighting and volume settings rather than under a neutral render.

title: Enhancement that cannot compound on itself
claim: The on-demand enhancer comments the original prompt into the same buffer with `#!PROMPT!:` and re-enhances from the comment, so re-running never enhances an enhancement; `@` appends to enhancer instructions where `@@` replaces them.

title: Change admission by implementer interest plus filed downstream obligations
claim: A change is admitted when at least two implementers are interested and none opposed, with tests, a bug filed per engine, both accessibility mapping specifications, and the documentation issue all filed as part of admission.

title: Widening what a call forwards widens what its cache must key on
claim: Adding a forwarded parameter to a call silently makes its cache key incomplete.

title: Assert variance: a metric with two possible outputs is a placeholder
claim: A metric that can only ever produce two values across all inputs is a placeholder, and a test should assert variance.

title: A background-flush store needs an explicit flush before a reopen read
claim: A store that flushes in the background must be flushed explicitly before a test reopens it to read back.

title: A per-file denylist of known-wrong API names, with a negative lookbehind
claim: Documentation is checked against a per-file denylist of API names known to be wrong, with a negative lookbehind so a legitimate neighbour does not trip it.

title: Validate doc code blocks against the support floor, not the dev runtime
claim: Documentation code blocks are validated against the declared minimum supported runtime rather than against whatever the developer has installed.

title: Narrow a platform exemption with a positive failure marker
claim: A platform-specific exemption skips the known noise rather than the whole class, by requiring a positive marker of the expected failure.

title: Adversarial-identity fixtures, mandated for identity and state refactors
claim: A test-only invariant assertion plus adversarial-identity fixtures are mandated for any refactor touching identity or state.

title: The unwaivable check guards the class with zero incidents
claim: An override asymmetry leaves the one check that cannot be waived protecting the class of issue that has never caused an incident.

title: A waiver token with thirteen accepted synonyms cannot be audited
claim: The waiver token accepts thirteen spellings (pass, manual-pass, manual, approved, accepted, allow-warnings, ...), so no count of waivers is trustworthy.

title: Provenance is recorded; relationships are not
claim: based_on is filled in 190 of 193 records while related is filled in 15, so the relational graph the specification promises does not exist.

title: No attributable entity means the guard goes global
claim: A shell command's side effects are attributable to no path, so it takes a single global guard while per-path writes run in parallel.

title: A probe that can never settle must not gate first paint
claim: A rival harness hangs forever awaiting an OSC 11 answer its terminal never sends - 148 bytes out, no UI, bricked in any non-mainstream terminal.

title: The tool schema is a scheduling contract
claim: The shell tool's JSON schema documents its per-path locking behaviour so the model batches independent calls in one turn and serializes same-file ones.

title: Bump the wire protocol once per publication boundary
claim: Bump the protocol version once per publication boundary, not once per incompatible change, and do not bump again for multiple incompatible changes before that protocol is published.

title: An ongoing estimate beside a settled truth
claim: A wallet carries two balances - a flag-and-drain ongoing estimate flagged on every ingested event and drained by a clock, and a settled truth - and the clock's cache gate is a cost gate, not a correctness one.

title: Re-read the record one statement before the network call
claim: The invoice is re-read one statement before the provider call because the three provider round-trips are themselves the staleness window.

title: An edition flag inside the pricing model
claim: A licence check inside the percentage charge model changes one fixture's price from 301.691 to 16.142 - pricing behaviour gated on an edition flag.

title: A quorum of occurrences before an entry is matchable
claim: Require a minimum number of independent occurrences before an entry becomes eligible for semantic matching, so a single crafted question cannot become an attractor.

title: A detector over a mixed population is tuned until inert
claim: Sending the whole prompt as one undifferentiated block makes the filter evaluate your own system instructions as potential attacks, producing false positives that push teams to lower the threshold until the filter does nothing.

title: Tiered logging by content sensitivity
claim: Three sinks with their own retention and access policies - metadata at about 1 KB, hashed content at about 3 KB, sampled full fidelity - instead of one log level.

title: Configuration divergence in a failover region is silent
claim: Drift between the primary and failover configurations is silent and behavioral - the same input is blocked in one region and allowed in the other - and failing into a region holding no reservation throttles under exactly the conditions that caused the failover.

title: Snapshot configuration at entry so one turn cannot span two configs
claim: Evaluate flags once at the start of the request and carry the result through the turn, so a flag flipped mid-generation cannot produce a response assembled from two configurations.

title: A schema reference to a network URI inside a tool definition
claim: A $ref to a network URI inside a tool definition is a server-side-request-forgery primitive, and the spec pairs it with a fail-closed rule for unresolvable refs.

title: An argument mirrored into an HTTP header
claim: An x-mcp-header extension mirrors a tool argument into an HTTP header under a MUST-reconcile-or-reject rule, which puts model-composed strings into the routing fabric; two readers found this independently.

title: Strong consistency on mint, eventual on mutate
claim: The protocol demands strong consistency for minting an identity and accepts eventual consistency for mutating it.

title: Authenticate before any attacker-triggerable outbound request
claim: Fetch client metadata only after authenticating the user, generalized: do not make an attacker-triggerable outbound request before you know who asked.

title: An enforcement claim about the system's shape
claim: A skill claims zero per-engine dispatch points and that main.py requires zero changes, contradicted by four engine comparison chains, while the one machine-enforced registration point is a schema regex listed as one bullet among fifteen.

title: Few-shot examples delivered as real conversation turns
claim: Few-shot examples are delivered as real conversation turns rather than inline prompt text, because small models echo an inline example's output for unrelated inputs.

title: Two measurement lanes that never share a fixture
claim: The paper reproduction harness and the product test suite deliberately never share a fixture.

title: First implementation is the long pole
claim: Specification to first implementation has a mean of 1 year 9 months and a median of 7 days, versus 5 months 10 days for first to second implementation (n about 9), so incentives must reward being first rather than punish being last.

title: Own the validation to own the error policy
claim: Transcode with replacement characters and then disable the dependency's own checker, because its policy on invalid input is to abort the file.

title: A read-only tool's guarantee is its most valuable property
